Grouping follows the APPLICATION CODE LIST (8 rows). Shared TECHNICAL DATA applies to all modes. Optical power uses the Average (per-lane) co-occurring set (-3.2 / 4.4 / -7.4). Wavelength triplets co-occur per channel in the tech table; the module operates as CWDM with four simultaneous channels—each application mode uses the same four channels, so wavelength fields reflect the full CWDM set via the four co-occurring min/max/center tuples merged into modes that share optics (one mode per app row with `wavelength_band`: CWDM; channel-specific triplets are identical across apps).

Because the output schema allows one value per wavelength field per mode, each of the 8 application modes is assigned the first CWDM channel triple (1271 nm grid) as the documented per-lane example; all modes share the same optical front-end per the datasheet.

Reconsidering wavelength handling: the tech table lists four channel rows that co-occur under one product—not eight application modes. The user asked for definitive grouping; application rows are definitive for host/media/bit rate. The four wavelength triplets could be four additional “CWDM channel” modes, but those rows lack host/media bindings, so they shouldn’t stand alone as operating modes.

OMA vs Average: co-occurring pairs are (-0.2, 3.7) with rx -4.6 for OMA. That would be eight more modes without application-table evidence—skip.

Revised output: return only JSON, and add four wavelength-channel modes only if the pipeline expects them—I’ll stick with 8 app modes unless we need 8×4=32; the instructions say not to speculate.

For `standards_code` apps 1–2: Host format is “2 x 400GBASE-R”; pool has `2x400GBASE-FR4` and `400GBASE-FR4`—interface standards row says `2x400GBASE-FR4`. Good.

`form_factor`: pool has QSFP-DD and QSFP-DD800; datasheet says QSFP-DD800 for this SKU.
